chapter: Politics, bebop and the small-band years
title: African-themed tunes and tom-tom ballads of the late 1930s
summary: Crouch asks about pieces with African titles and mallets on tom-toms, and Crawford vaguely recalls playing such rhythms.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh, I know what I was going to ask you. There was a period in the late '30s, Rex Stewart was talking about it, late '30s and '40s, when there was --
You mention Rex quite a bit. You must know him --
Well, he wrote a lot, you know. Rex wrote a lot of essays about the '30s. In fact, --
In fact, I'll tell you what. Next time I see this book he wrote, called Jazz Masters of the 1930's, I'll get you a copy.
Thank you. Tell him Jimmy Crawford wants it. And he knows I will try my utmost to read it.
Well, he was saying that there was a period where people were writing a lot of tunes and had a African titles and references to it, like (he did one called "Menelik") (singing). Anyway, --
Did you ever play those kind of pieces,
used mallets like pieces, ballads on the tom-toms and stuff like -- he said it was based in the late '30s. Do you remember any of that?
I'm pretty sure I did, but I don't remember what-all I did. Which was very little, at that. But I got a effect of it, and I liked it. Used to play those rhythms, (Sambas,) Latin types.
